1. W star moved from (6, 17) to (11, 24) - moved down-right
2. O diamond moved from (12, 25) to (14, 27) - moved down-right
3. Both changed shape (new hashes, different pixel counts)
The W star seems to have moved closer to O, and O moved further from its original position. This is similar to level 1 where clicking p's M center caused objects to shift.
Looking at the ascii:
Row 10: BBBBBBBBBBBBWBBBBB - W at col 23
Row 11: BBBBBBBBBBBWWWBBBB - W at cols 22-24
Row 12: BBBBBBBBBBWWOOOOBB - W at cols 21-22, O at cols 23-26
Row 13: BBBBBBBBBBBWOOOOOw - W at col 22, O at cols 23-27
Row 14: BBBBBBBBBBBBOOMOOB - O at cols 24-27, M at col 26
Row 15: BBBBBBBBBBwwOOOOOB - O at cols 24-27
Row 16: BBBBBBBBwwBBBOOOBB - O at cols 27-29
So W and O are now overlapping/merged. W is at (10-13, 21-24) and O is at (12-16, 23-29).
This is similar to level 1 where clicking p's M center caused W to merge with p. The pattern seems to be:
- Click trigger object's M center → objects merge/shift
In level 1, after this merge, I needed to:
1. Click objects to swap them
2. Click ring to pull object to ring
Let me try clicking on one of the G diamonds to see if it swaps with something. Or maybe I should click the ring directly.
Actually, let me think about the level 1 solution more carefully:
1. Initial state: W at ring, p below, G below p
2. Clicked p's M center → W fell from ring
3. Clicked ring → W pulled to ring
4. Clicked p's M center → W fell again
5. Clicked p's purple pixel → W fell and merged with p
6. Clicked G's center → G and W swapped
7. Clicked ring → G pulled to ring, level completed
So the key was to get G (dark gray) to the top position (closest to ring), then click ring.

Let me try clicking the ring (41, 49).
